title: Onramp checklist and success hypotheses — Emberline retail pilot
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the minimal onramp checklist, measurable success hypotheses, and the initial workshop agenda for the Emberline retail POC. The goal is to validate a production-ready recommendation+conversational flow powered by Redwood inference within an 8-week window and to produce a clear go/no-go recommendation for next steps (Dedicated vs Hosted + integration scope).

Scope (what we will deliver in PoC):
- Integrate Emberline product feed (structured catalog: SKUs, attrs, inventory) with Redwood hosted inference endpoints.
- Deploy a conversational recommender pipeline for 2 user journeys: product discovery and post-purchase support.
- Instrument quality and cost telemetry via Redwood Console dashboards.
- Run synthetic and shadow traffic A/B comparisons vs Emberline current heuristic system.
- Produce acceptance report with latency/cost/quality tradeoffs and recommended deployment mode.

Out of scope (for this PoC):
- Full checkout or payment integration.
- Multi-region high-availability (single region only).
- Custom model training — will use curated open model variants only.

Primary success hypotheses (quantitative + qualitative):
1) Latency & Reliability hypothesis: conversational responses (end-to-end) will meet 95th percentile latency < 300ms for short-form queries and < 700ms for longer contextual dialogs in the hosted environment under baseline load (50 RPS).
   - Metric: 95th pct latency measured in Redwood Console; target: <300ms (single-turn product suggestions).
   - Acceptance: pass if both latency and error-rate <1.5% sustained for 48h load test.
2) Quality hypothesis: intent classification + slot extraction F1 >= 0.88 on Emberline annotated dev set and user satisfaction score >= 4/5 in manual eval (n=50).
   - Metric: automated F1 from labeled test set + human rating of diverse dialogues.
3) Business impact hypothesis: recommendation conversations increase click-to-details rate by >= 12% relative to baseline heuristics in shadow mode.
   - Metric: CTR uplift in A/B shadow run (2M impressions sample or 7-day window).
4) Cost hypothesis: per-1k active sessions inference cost (tokens + infra) can be kept <= $X (TBD after perf run) when applying suggested batching/caching profile.

Acceptance criteria (must all be met for sign-off):
- All three quantitative hypotheses (latency, quality, business impact) pass or have documented remediation plan + re-run timeline agreed with customer.
- Security & data handling checklist completed and signed (see security items below).
- Integration tests pass: end-to-end flows in staging with sample product feed and webhook playback.
- Observability: dashboards instrumented for token-level cost, 95/99 latency, error classes, and per-route throughput.

Milestones & timeline (8-week plan):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): alignment workshop, data access, key roles, and sandbox credentials exchange.
- Week 1: sample data ingestion + schema mapping, quick local end-to-end smoke test.
- Week 2: API integration and adapter layer; first Canary conversation flow in staging.
- Week 3: Quality tuning (prompt sets, reranking), human eval batch 1.
- Week 4: Load testing (50–200 RPS window), cost profiling, collect perf telemetry.
- Week 5: Shadow run against heuristic recommender for live CTR monitoring.
- Week 6: Final quality iterations, additional evals, and drift checks.
- Week 7: Prepare acceptance report and decision review, internal dry run.
- Week 8: Customer review and sign-off; produce recommendations for Dedicated vs Hosted and next steps.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Customer PM (Emberline): data access, business metrics, acceptance signoff.
- Redwood solutions lead: Aisha Patel — technical integration owner, workshop facilitation, acceptance author.
- Redwood SRE: Marcus Li — infra config, VPC peering, load testing.
- Redwood ML engineer: Rosa Kim — prompt engineering, eval design, quality metrics.
- Data engineer (customer): Diego Alvarez — catalog export, sample dataset, mapping support.

Workshop agenda (90m Kickoff, Week 0):
- 0–10m: Intros + success definition (Aisha)
- 10–25m: Emberline product + data overview (Customer PM)
- 25–40m: Integration constraints (SRE + infra)
- 40–60m: Success metrics deep dive (quality, latency, CTR) and acceptance rubric
- 60–80m: Risks & mitigation, stretch goals, decision gates
- 80–90m: Next steps + ownership + immediate actions (who does what by when)

Integration & infra checklist (must be ready before Week1 integration):
- [ ] Catalog export API token (read-only) provided to Redwood sandbox.
- [ ] Sample dataset: 5k SKUs with descriptions, attributes, images URLs, price, inventory.
- [ ] VPC peering + firewall rules for staging (if customer requests Private control plane).
- [ ] TLS certs / key management plan (KMS/HSM) — documented.
- [ ] GDPR/PII review: confirm no PII in sample payloads or clear data policy.

Acceptance tests (executable/traceable):
- E2E smoke: user types “show me running shoes under $100” -> system returns top-5 relevant SKUs, response time < 300ms.
- Intent extraction: 100 labeled utterances -> F1 >= 0.88.
- Robustness: malformed input (typos, partial queries) -> graceful fallback with clarifying question < 2 turns.
- Load: 50 RPS sustained with <1.5% error rate and 95th-latency target met.

Risks & mitigations (quick notes):
- Data freshness: product feed latency may cause stale inventory. Mitigate: schedule hourly syncs and degrade to read-only cache when missing inventory fields.
- Cold-start latency for long context: enable prefix cache and short-history sessions for discovery flows.
- Cost overshoot during load tests: cap max tokens per response and enable capped batching.

Open questions / decisions to capture at kickoff:
- Customer target budget for per-1k sessions inference (we need an explicit dollar target to tune quantization/batching).
- Will Emberline accept hosted tokenization/embeddings or insist on private embeddings? (affects Private deployment scope).
- Which KPIs are non-negotiable for go/no-go? e.g., is CTR uplift required or is parity ok for demo?

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Bring sample prompt templates and a short manual eval rubric to the kickoff — Rosa will bring 40 labeled utterances.
- Prep firewall checklist for Marcus before workshop.
- Ask Sales to confirm contractual trial limits (RPS, duration) so we can shape load test plan.

Quick checklist for immediate pre-kickoff actions (owners):
- Emberline: share sample dataset + API token (due: +3 days)
- Redwood (Aisha): prepare workshop slides + acceptance rubric (due: +2 days)
- Redwood (Marcus): initial staging infra footprint + cost estimate (due: +4 days)

Sign-off rubric (final review):
- Green = all acceptance criteria pass and stakeholder signoff (customer PM + Redwood eng lead).
- Amber = at least one quantitative metric missed but with agreed remediation plan + timeline.
- Red = critical metric failed with no viable remediation in PoC timeframe.

Appendix / references:
- Related artifacts: CONF-4208 (detailed PoC spec), JIRA-1793 (integration ticket), PR-27 (adapter work in progress).
- Eval checklist shorthand: 50 human eval dialogues (diverse personas), 2 automated F1 runs, 48h load validation window, CTR shadow run 7d or 2M impressions.

---
This is intentionally concise; capture any deviations during kickoff in the meeting minutes and push updates into the Confluence page linked above.
